svg.text: F-D ZUSTAND — change the state first, then handle rigid bodies
A −25 °C contact plate makes soft meat and mince rigid in 2–4 min; then a plain gripper, trays and one blade do the rest.
bay 1000 W × 600 D · 14 actuators
cold clamp 300 × 200, −25 °C, ~250 W compressor
3 mm crust in ~100 s (Plank)
all food-contact parts are loose: 8–12 per meal to the wash
SIDE VIEW of the bay (schematic, about 1 px per mm)
X-Y-Z gantry under a drip hood
COLD CLAMP −25 °C
(Zone S: never touches food)

100 s: 3 mm frozen crust each face

classic three trays

rigid: held by one edge like a plate
30–60 s in air: tacky film for the flour
turned over by rotating the gripper
pressed into the crumbs at 30 N
crust thaws in the pan
Why it is fast: contact freezing

g.text: The plate, not the freezer, is the tool: a 180 g slice needs ~200 W.

svg.text: Ice-cube-tray forming (S17)
Elsewhere and weak points

g.text: Same idea elsewhere: band knife slices a tempered block one slice at a
time; Rouladen seam ice-welded on the plate (S16); skins slip after
steam or blanch in a rubber-finger drum (S12).
Cleaning: the cold plate is Zone S (defrosted daily); trays, moulds,
cradles and fingers go to the wash chamber.
Weak point: every soft item waits 2–4 min on one plate (queueing);
customers may dislike surface-frozen fresh meat.

svg.text: 1/7 A limp raw cutlet on a thin steel tray is laid on the cold clamp; the upper plate closes
2/7 Both faces at −25 °C: in about 100 s each face has a 3 mm frozen crust
3/7 The cutlet is now a rigid plate: a simple two-finger gripper holds it by one edge
4/7 Classic breading: flour, egg, crumbs — dipped like a solid part
5/7 Turned over by rotating the gripper, pressed into the crumbs
6/7 Laid into the hot pan; the thin frozen crust thaws as it browns
7/7 Nothing fixed touched food; tray and gripper fingers go to the wash chamber
